title: Dual-stage semantic-rank model admission and profile publish
creator: Asha Kumar
description: Admit a dual-stage model bundle (embedding encoder + pairwise reranker) into the model catalog, produce and publish a deterministic performance profile, and pin a versioned manifest suitable for Dedicated and Private deployments. This ticket covers: (1) admission criteria checklist (accuracy baseline, memory/kv-cache footprint, supported ops/kernels), (2) automated performance harness runs for throughput and P99 latency at representative sequence lengths, (3) generation of a pinning manifest that binds model weights, quantization profile, and kernel hints, and (4) publishable profile artifacts (JSON + human-readable summary) and CI gating to prevent regressions. We must ensure runtime compatibility with existing kernel set, recommend quantization/packing options for Dedicated, and add smoke tests for canary rollouts. This is a companion to onboarding flow work; it focuses on edge-case stability and measurable profiles for reranker latency under batched traffic.
acceptance_criteria: Model bundle successfully ingested into staging catalog with generated manifest and unique pinned version
Performance profile published to /catalog/profiles with P50/P95/P99 latency and throughput curves for 1/4/8 and 32 item batches
Automated CI step compares new profile to baseline and flags >10% P99 regression
Quantization recommendation included (FP16 or 8-bit) and verified in smoke harness with <2% hit on reranker top-1 recall
Canary rollout plan created and verified via synthetic traffic; rollback hook implemented
progress_updates: 2025-02-17: Kickoff sync with PM and research. Agreed admission checklist items and minimum eval set (100 labelled queries from retrieval benchmark).

2025-02-21: Added kernel-compat unit to harness; discovered two unsupported fused-attention ops in the reranker graph—filed ENG-24612 to sketch kernel shim. Blocking until kernel shim landed for deterministic runs.

2025-02-26: Initial embedding encoder profile run completed in single-GPU staging. Observed KV cache growth beyond expected baseline at long seq (512 tokens); added memory sampling to harness and lowered batch target for P99 test.

2025-02-28: PR opened for manifest generator that captures model hash + quant profile + runtime hints: https://github.com/redwood-inference/catalog/pull/178. Feedback from runtime team: include 'fallback_variant' field for Hosted graceful degradation.
2025-03-02: Reranker micro-benchmark results: baseline top-1 recall 0.82, quantized FP16 run 0.81. PM accepted 1% drop trade-off for 2x throughput improvement. Preparing profile publication draft.

2025-03-03: Integration tests green on staging except one flaky case under high concurrent batches (>128 concurrent requests) found by stress runner. Triage step added to isolate scheduling contention.
qa_plan: Run perf harness against three staging instance types (g4dn, a10g, a100) and record token/sec, memory, P50/P95/P99 for 1000 synthetic queries
Functional eval: run 100 labelled queries and assert reranker recall >= 0.80 baseline
Stability: 30-minute soak at target throughput for each batch size (1/8/32) and capture rejection/error rates
Compatibility: verify manifest-replay produces identical inference graph on runtime-1.22 with kernel hints applied
Security: ensure model artifact storage path uses customer KMS policy when onboarding a private bundle (step-by-step documented)
rollout_plan: Publish profile to staging catalog and run full CI gating (unit + perf + stability).
Create canary release to <5 customers> on Dedicated for two weeks with telemetry dashboards enabled (cost and P99 latency).
If metrics within thresholds (P99 < target +10% and error rate < 0.1%), proceed to wider Dedicated rollout and list as Hosted-compat fallback variant.
Automate rollback to previous pinned version via console rollout controls if telemetry shows regression.
notes: Trade-offs: we accepted a small top-1 recall drop (<=1%) to enable a quantized profile that halves memory and doubles throughput on T4-like hardware.
Risk: scheduling contention under high concurrency needs a runtime fix—tracked in ENG-24618. Consider temporary throttle at routing layer if fix delayed.
Follow-ups: add a dedicated export format for profile curves (CSV + JSON) so product analytics can ingest token-cost curves in console.

Artifacts: PRs - runtime shim PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/5172, catalog manifest PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/catalog/pull/178, perf-run notebook https://drive.google.com/drive/fake/perf-notebook-ENg24601
